title: vehicle-sil simulation configuration (simulation.yaml), format 1
description: The networks and the participants (ECU executables) of one simulation, for vehicle_sil_launch check, run and test. This schema finds unknown keys, missing keys and values of the wrong form while you write. It cannot see the executables: whether the names, the steps, the networks and the variables fit them is what `vehicle_sil_launch check <file>` says, and so is everything else this schema leaves open (a key written twice, names listed twice, combinations of keys, the arguments of a command). The manual is docs/simulation-config.md of vehicle-sil.

stop_at_ms.description: The virtual time at which the simulation stops, in milliseconds. Without it, the simulation runs until a participant stops it or until run is stopped (Ctrl+C). With time_step_ms, it must be a multiple of time_step_ms.

start_timeout_ms.description: How long run waits for the required participants to join, in milliseconds.

stop_timeout_ms.description: How long run waits for each participant to end, in milliseconds, at each stage of stopping.

registry_uri.description: Where run starts the registry of the simulation: silkit://<host>:<port>, with a port from 1 to 65535. Without it, a free port on 127.0.0.1. For participants on other computers too, an address they reach (silkit://0.0.0.0:8500); the simulation then listens on the network, where anyone who reaches this computer can join.

speed.description: How fast virtual time passes: simulation seconds per wall-clock second (1: real time, 2: twice as fast, 0.5: half as fast), or max. Without it, as fast as possible. run --speed overrides it.

time_step_ms.description: The step of the launcher's controller, in milliseconds of virtual time: how finely the simulation can be paused, stepped and paced. Without it, the launcher chooses one (10 at full speed). stop_at_ms must be a multiple of it.

late_tolerance_ms.description: How late a step may begin, in wall-clock milliseconds, before it counts as late (when a speed is given).

networks.description: Every network the ECUs use. May be empty.

name.description: The network's name: the one the ECUs give to j1939(), can(), lin_master(), lin_slave() or ethernet().

participants.description: The participants of the simulation: the ECU executables, and other executables that join it.

name.description: The participant's name, on one line, not starting with '-'. An ecu_main executable gets it with --name. SimulationController is taken (the launcher's controller).

command.description: The executable and its arguments. A relative path counts from this file's directory; a name without / is also looked up on PATH. On Windows, .exe may be left out.

step_ms.description: The step the executable reports, in milliseconds. Compared only when written (and only with describe: true).

describe.description: true: an executable made with ecu_main; check asks it what it is (--describe) and compares. false: any other executable; it is not checked, and its command may use the placeholders "{registry_uri}" and "{name}".

required.description: Whether the simulation waits for this participant. false only with describe: false (a tool that only listens, such as a logger). At least one participant that is not left out must be required.

enabled.description: false leaves the participant out: it is neither checked nor started. --disable and --enable override it for one run.

manual.description: true: you start this participant yourself (from a debugger, for example); run prints the command and waits for it. --manual does the same for one run.

role.description: What the participant is for; only check reads it, a run is the same for every role. ecu: an ECU of the vehicle. test: a participant for testing (a spy, a tool that talks to the ECUs); it does not count as an ECU of a network. bridge: it carries networks to real buses; check warns of a test participant with J1939 nodes on a network that a bridge may carry. Variants cannot change it.

variants.description: The variants of the simulation: each name with what it changes of the common part above. A file with variants needs --variant <name> for check and run; test runs them all.

propertyNames.description: A variant's name: a text on one line that does not start with '-' (it is given with --variant).

params.description: Values of the parameters that scenarios use as ${name}. They replace the defaults a scenario gives in its own params; a variant's params and --param replace these.

oneOf.description: The executable alone (the text is not split at spaces).
The executable, then its arguments, one item each. Write a placeholder in quotes ("{registry_uri}").

variables.description: The variable map: the names the simulation uses (the keys), each with the executable's variable behind it. For executables whose variables differ in name, unit or values; a variable that is not listed is seen under the executable's own name.

variable.description: One of: the executable's name of the variable (renames it); { from, scale, offset } (the value seen is the executable's value * scale + offset); { from, map } (names for its values); { absent: true } (this executable does not have it).

from.description: The executable's name of the variable.

scale.description: The value seen is the executable's value * scale + offset. Not 0. For an integer or a real variable; the variable seen is a real. Not together with map.

offset.description: The value seen is the executable's value * scale + offset. Not together with map.

map.description: Names for the executable's values (whole numbers), one name a value. For an integer or an enum variable; the variable seen is an enum with these items only. Not together with scale or offset.

unit.description: The unit of the value seen.

absent.description: This executable does not have the variable: the scenario steps that use it are skipped. Takes no other key.

not.description: scale and offset convert a number, map names the values: one of the two.

propertyNames.description: A parameter's name: letters, digits and _ (not a digit first).

additionalProperties.description: One value: a number, true or false, or a text. It cannot use another parameter (${...}).

variant.description: What this variant changes of the common part; {} (or nothing) for the common part as it is.

participants.description: The participants of the common part that differ in this variant, by name. A participant of this variant only is listed in the common part with enabled: false, and gets enabled: true here.

command.description: The executable and its arguments, instead of the common command (the whole of it).

variables.description: Variable mappings laid over the common ones: a mapping of the same name replaces the common one, another name is added.

enabled.description: Whether the participant is in this variant, instead of the common enabled.

params.description: Parameters laid over the common params, name by name.
